etc_dir.description: Path to the AFS configuration directory.

bin_dir.description: Path to AFS binaries and support scripts.

num_threads.description: Number of threads used by the fileserver for handling I/O requests. Adjust based on CPU/core count and workload.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of concurrent connections the fileserver will accept.

listen_addr.description: IP address the fileserver binds to. Use a specific IP to restrict access.

fileserver_port.description: UDP/TCP port used by the fileserver for client communication.

cmserver_port.description: Port used for cache manager communication (typically with the volume server).

root_dir.description: Top-level mount point for AFS namespace.

volumes_dir.description: Local directory (partition) where AFS volumes are stored.

backup_dir.description: Directory used for backup-related temporary files (if backup is enabled).

backup_enabled.description: Enable backup server integration (required only if running backup services on this node).

kerberos_principal.description: Kerberos service principal for authentication (e.g., 'afs/afs.example.com@EXAMPLE.COM'). Leave empty to disable Kerberos.

items.description: Hostname or IP address of an AFS database (CellServDB) server.

cell_servers.description: List of cell database servers (e.g., vlserver, kaserver, ptserver). Must include at least one reachable server.

items.description: Name of an AFS cell to trust for cross-cell access (must be defined in /etc/openafs/CellServDB).

trusted_cells.description: List of additional AFS cells to trust for inter-cell volume mounts.

items.description: Command-line argument to pass to the fileserver binary (e.g., '-nojumbo', '-n'.)

extra_args.description: Extra startup options for the fileserver (space-separated when rendered).

debug.description: Enable verbose debug logging (for troubleshooting only).
